correctness.rationale: For distinct primes p,q and integer t>=2, set e=2^t and b=e/2 even. Reconstructed sigma**(r^{2b})=(r^b-1)(r^{b+1}+1)/(r-1), tau**(r^{2b})=2b. Harmonic divisibility would force (p^2+1) B |2e p^2 q^e, B=(q^b-1)(q^{b+1}+1)/(q-1). Because b even, both (q^b-1)/(q-1) and q^{b+1}+1 vanish mod q+1, hence (q+1)^2|B. For q=2, (p^2+1)/2 has a forbidden odd divisor; for p=2, q=5 from p^2+1=5 but q+1 forces forbidden factor 3. For odd primes, odd divisor of p^2+1 implies q|p^2+1 and q=1 mod4; m=(q+1)/2 odd has m^2|p^2 (by (q+1)^2 and coprime support), forcing m=p and q=2p-1. Mod q, 4(p^2+1)=(q+1)^2+4 gives q|5, hence p=3,q=5. Then 5^{b+1}+1 >=126 cannot divide the 2*3^2 factor (its 2-adic order=1), contradiction. Independent exact prime-pair finite calculations corroborate 2310 combinations; the unrestricted proof is the divisor argument.
